cluster_name: Dutch court sentences Dutch-Rwandan man for 1994 Rwanda genocide role
event_summary: A Dutch court in The Hague on 28 August 2026 sentenced Eugene N., a 66-year-old Dutch-Rwandan national, to life in prison for war crimes and genocide committed during the 1994 Rwanda genocide, including directing a massacre of 3,000 Tutsis at a football stadium in Mbazi. His defence plans to appeal.
tldr: Ten outlets across ten countries covered Friday's Dutch verdict in near-identical factual terms — no outlet broke from the crime-and-punishment template to editorialize about international justice norms or Dutch-Rwandan relations. The sharpest editorial variance was lexical: NL Times, the sole Netherlands-based outlet, was the only source to describe Eugene N. as having 'orchestrated' the massacre, attributing deliberate agency where all others settled for 'involvement' or 'participation'. Rwanda itself — the country whose government issued the original 2014 extradition request and whose courts have prosecuted hundreds of genocide perpetrators — is absent from the corpus, leaving the voices most directly shaped by the genocide unrepresented. Le Devoir is the only outlet to surface the extradition bar that required the Netherlands to conduct its own trial rather than transfer Eugene N. to Kigali.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only outlet to call Eugene N. the 'orchestrator' of the massacre, framing his role as command-level rather than participation.
Reports Eugene N.'s age as 67, while all nine other outlets report 66 — a minor factual discrepancy with no identified source.
Only outlet to reproduce the prosecutor's direct rhetorical address to the court, adding courtroom detail absent from all other summaries.
Only outlet to explicitly note Eugene N. was acquitted on the incitement to genocide count, providing legal nuance no other outlet included.
Covers the genocide conviction with no editorial framing, immigration angle, or broader European political context — an unusually neutral treatment for this outlet.

bottom_line: Coverage of the Dutch life sentence for the 1994 Rwanda genocide is unanimous and uniform across 10 outlets spanning 10 countries — every outlet treats it as a factual criminal-justice proceeding with no divergent framing. Rwanda itself is absent from the corpus despite the verdict directly concerning a 2014 Rwandan extradition request, leaving the country most affected by the genocide without a documented voice in international coverage.
